title.narrative: Civil Aviation Development Investment Program, Tranche 3

description.narrative: The Tranche 3 will continue from Tranches 1 and 2, to establish a sustainable civil aviation network to support the economic growth of the country. Tranche 3 will further strengthen and sustain the operations of National Airports Cooperation (NAC), PNG Air Services Limited (PNG ASL), and Civil Aviation Safety Authority of PNG (CASAPNG). The national airports have low level of compliance with safety and security standards, creating risks of accidents and illegal movements of people and goods. The air-side runway pavements, terminal buildings and utilities are in poor condition.Tranche 3 will improve and upgrade nine national airports including pavement strengthening, runway extensions, security fencing, apron extensions, fire stations, traffic control tower and terminal buildings. In addition, runway lights at seven airports, runway security fencing at three other airports and new market sheds will be constructed for women to promote local artifacts.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President
Reports and Recommendations of the President
Loan 3496: 100% of contracts awarded and 100% disbursed as of 25 Nov 2024
Loan 3497: 100% of contracts awarded and 100% disbursed as of 25 Nov 2024

Progress Toward Outcome: Procurement is ongoing for contract packages under the tranche. The Momote Airport Pavement Upgrade and Terminal Building and Mt. Hagen Pavement Strengthening and Upgrade both procured under advance contracting are now under construction. Since January 2018, ADB has approved and awarded five (5) more packages under the tranche; for Gurney and Mendi Airport Upgrades and a fencing package comprising 3 contracts for Kerema, Kiunga and Tari. Gurney works have commenced while Mendi Airport Upgrade is still awaiting mobilization of the contractor who has been delayed due to political unrest at the project location. The three (3) fencing contracts are at present also preparing to mobilize to the respective sites. The remaining packages under the tranche (5 Works, 1 Goods and Consulting Services) are at various stages of procurement. ADB on 18 September issued approval of the BER for Vanimo Airport Runway Extension. Contract signing is anticipated around October 2018. A revised procurement plan submitted by the EA is currently being reviewed for approval. The EA has excluded the scope for the airfield lighting system and replaced the Buka Airport upgrade with a new works package for Wapenamanda Airport New Terminal Building and Associated Works. The revised procurement plan will be submitted for approval in PRS once finalized.
Some results are in the Audited Project Financial Statements | Aug 2023: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/43141/43141-044-apfs-en_3.pdf
Some results are in the Social Monitoring Reports | Feb 2023: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/43141/43141-043-43141-044-smr-en_6.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: 1. The three entities, NAC, PNGASL and CASAPNG are getting ongoing support under the investment program on improving airport facilities and institutional capacity development to strengthen their regulatory roles.
2. Procurement is ongoing for contract packages for airport covered under this tranche and will comply to ICAO standards by 2019 when these contracts are fully completed.
3. The investment program is assisting in the ongoing upgrade of the existing infrastructures to improve airport operations. Tranche 3 has 12 contract packages; 10 for airport works upgrade and 1 for airport lighting system and Consulting Services. Four of the works packages and a fencing package (split into 3 contracts) have been awarded while the remaining packages are at different stages of procurement.
